- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

## Executive view

The Seller package materially departs from the Buyer playbook. The principal problems are:

1. an unauthorised reduction of the general warranty cap and claim period;
2. materially inflated thresholds and an excess-only basket;
3. an attempt to apply the general limitations regime to title, indemnities, covenants and all other claims;
4. no effective fraud/deliberate misconduct carve-out;
5. deemed disclosure of the entire data room and public records;
6. an overbroad Buyer-knowledge exclusion;
7. inadequate completion protection for Bluefen and Riverlark;
8. incomplete treatment of bonuses and Ironquay IP; and
9. assertions that Tax/IP and other matters are “settled” when they remain open.

Labels such as **[STANDARD]**, “cleared by both sides”, “market standard” and “agreed” carry no authority. The Disclosure Letter itself appropriately says that it contains no negotiation approval. We should review and mark up the entire package, including every provision labelled [STANDARD].

## Detailed issues and recommended pushback

### 1. General warranty cap

**Seller position:** 20% / AUD 4.8 million.

**Departure:** Our starting position is 25% / AUD 6 million. The 20% fallback may be used only with Amelia Frost’s prior written authority identifying the draft. No such authority has been given.

**Pushback:** Reinstate a 25% / AUD 6 million general warranty cap. Do not treat the matching fallback number as approval.

The cap must also apply only to the agreed general warranty category. It must not capture title, Tax, specific indemnities, payment obligations, covenants or fraud-related claims merely because the definition of “Claim” is broad.

---

### 2. De minimis and basket

**Seller position:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket; only the excess over the basket is recoverable.

**Departure:** Our position is:

- AUD 5,000 de minimis;
- AUD 50,000 aggregate basket; and
- a tipping basket, so the Seller is liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.

The Seller proposal is five times our thresholds and changes the basket from tipping to excess-only.

**Pushback:** Restore AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 with recovery from the first dollar after the basket is exceeded. Confirm that title/fundamental claims, fraud and relevant specific indemnities are outside both thresholds.

---

### 3. General warranty claim period

**Seller position:** 18 months.

**Departure:** Our position is 24 months. An 18-month fallback requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval, which has not been given.

**Pushback:** Restore 24 months after Completion. The Seller’s statement that limitation periods apply to “all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise” should be reversed: each claim category should have its own express regime, and no category should fall into the general regime by drafting default.

---

### 4. Fundamental, title, capacity and authority claims

**Seller position:** Same cap and limitation period as general warranties.

**Departure:** This is directly contrary to our playbook.

**Pushback:** Capacity, authority, title, ownership and encumbrance claims must have:

- a separate 100% purchase-price cap;
- a claim period of at least six years;
- no general de minimis or basket;
- no Buyer-knowledge defence; and
- no qualification through general disclosure.

The warranties should cover legal and beneficial ownership, the entire issued share capital, authority to sell, valid transfer and absence of encumbrances or third-party rights.

---

### 5. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct

**Seller position:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all claims of any nature.

**Departure:** The draft appears to place even fraud and deliberate wrongdoing within caps, thresholds, time limits and exclusive remedies. That is unacceptable.

**Pushback:** Add an overriding carve-out, to the maximum extent enforceable, for:

- fraud;
- fraudulent misrepresentation;
- wilful concealment; and
- deliberate misconduct.

The carve-out must override all caps, baskets, de minimis thresholds, time limits, knowledge exclusions, exclusive-remedy provisions and non-reliance language. It cannot be traded away.

---

### 6. Hidden extension of the general limitations regime

The Seller proposes that the general regime apply to “all Claims” unless expressly excluded. This creates a serious risk that a drafting omission subjects unrelated rights to the general cap, basket and 18-month period.

**Pushback:** Use an express liability matrix and keep separate:

- general warranties;
- title/fundamental warranties;
- Tax;
- IP;
- specific indemnities;
- purchase-price and funds-flow obligations;
- debt repayment obligations; and
- pre- and post-Completion covenants.

Payment obligations and covenant enforcement should not be recast as “Claims” subject to the warranty regime. Tax and IP remain open; we should not accept either that they are resolved or that they are necessarily unlimited.

---

### 7. Disclosure standard

**Seller position:** General disclosure of every matter contained or referred to in the electronic data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records.

**Departure:** Our playbook requires specific fair disclosure and rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.

**Pushback:**

- Delete paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2 as general deemed disclosure.
- Require each exception to identify the relevant warranty and disclose the matter with sufficient detail to allow a reasonable buyer to understand its nature, scope and reasonably foreseeable consequences.
- Do not treat information as disclosed merely because it is somewhere in a document, cross-reference or public record.
- State that disclosure qualifies warranties only, unless a particular provision expressly says otherwise. It must not satisfy a condition precedent, release debt, cure title, waive an indemnity or excuse a covenant.

The data-room cut-off is **5.00 pm on 22 September 2026**, which is stale relative to the current review. Require an updated index, refreshed specific disclosures and a signing/Completion bring-down. Updates must be reviewed rather than deemed accepted.

The individual disclosures contain useful factual cautions, but those cautions do not cure the underlying issues.

---

### 8. Buyer knowledge

**Seller position:** No claim for anything known by the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.

**Departure:** This is an expansive actual, imputed and constructive-knowledge bar. It effectively reinstates general disclosure through the knowledge clause.

**Pushback:** Delete the blanket exclusion. In particular, reject:

- knowledge attributed from all Buyer advisers;
- constructive knowledge;
- matters the Buyer “could” or “should” have discovered;
- deemed knowledge from the data room or public searches; and
- any duty on the Buyer to investigate the Seller’s warranties.

Any retained knowledge mechanism must be tightly drafted and cannot excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. Seller warranties qualified by Seller knowledge should identify named Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry.

---

### 9. Bluefen consent

**Facts disclosed:** Bluefen represents approximately AUD 3.6 million FY26 revenue, around 30%. No final written consent or evidence that the associated conditions have been satisfied has been provided.

**Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied when written consent is delivered.

**Departure:** Delivery alone is insufficient where the consent is conditional. Reasonable endeavours also leaves the Buyer exposed to loss of a material customer relationship.

**Pushback:** Make Completion conditional on:

1. an effective written Bluefen consent in an agreed form;
2. evidence that all conditions to that consent have been satisfied or irrevocably waived;
3. confirmation that the consent remains effective at Completion; and
4. no materially adverse amendments, concessions or payments without Buyer approval.

The condition should not be deemed satisfied merely on document delivery. The Buyer should control waiver of this condition and retain termination rights if it is not met by the long-stop date.

---

### 10. Riverlark debt and security

**Facts disclosed:** Approximately AUD 3.2 million remains outstanding; the facility has not been repaid and no final security discharge has been provided.

**Seller position:** Release after Completion.

**Departure:** This conflicts with the debt-free/cash-free acquisition basis and our requirement for direct repayment and effective releases at Completion. “Approximately” is not adequate for funds flow.

**Pushback:** Require:

- a current lender payout letter close to Completion;
- repayment directly from Completion funds, with the amount reducing or coming from Seller proceeds;
- repayment of all principal, accrued interest, break costs and fees;
- effective releases and discharges of all guarantees and security at Completion; and
- appropriate filings and control-document deliveries.

A post-Completion release is not acceptable absent an irrevocable lender undertaking in an approved form and Amelia Frost’s express approval. No such approval presently exists.

---

### 11. Employee Completion bonuses

**Facts disclosed:** AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses; no treatment of payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs; no amount in the funds flow.

**Seller position:** A Seller matter, not separately itemised.

**Risk:** If the Company pays after Completion, the economic burden may silently pass to the Buyer even though the liability arose from the sale.

**Pushback:** Require the bonuses and all triggered employer on-costs to be:

- specifically itemised in the Completion statement/funds flow; and
- funded by the Seller, deducted from Seller proceeds or reimbursed under a specific indemnity.

Confirm which continued-employment conditions will be satisfied at Completion, the identity and amount for each recipient, payment timing and all payroll tax, superannuation and withholding consequences. Avoid double counting with Debt or working-capital mechanics, but do not allow the item to disappear from the economics.

---

### 12. Ironquay IP

**Facts disclosed:** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but this is not independent verification; there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment.

**Seller position:** Narrow indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment.

**Departure:** Payment alone may not establish that Paperbark owns or may use all relevant IP. The AUD 180,000 figure is not verified.

**Pushback:**

- Obtain direct/current verification of the amount payable.
- Require payment and delivery of an effective assignment or confirmation of ownership/licence as the contractual cure.
- Broaden the indemnity to cover failure to obtain the SOW3 rights, ownership/use defects, third-party claims, additional fees, enforcement and reasonable remediation losses.
- Preserve the SOW3 cure so that the Seller has an opportunity to procure the intended rights, subject to urgency and Buyer control protections.
- Ensure the indemnity is not inadvertently captured by the general warranty cap, basket or period.

The ultimate IP cap and duration remain open; we should not imply agreement to unlimited liability.

---

### 13. Export/privacy incident

**Facts disclosed:** A download link was sent to an unintended external email address and may relate to about 1,240 records. Access, exact scope, notification obligations and loss are not established.

The disclosure is appropriately cautious. We should neither accept the Seller’s assertion that the matter is immaterial nor characterise it as a confirmed breach.

**Pushback:** Require the Seller and Company to:

- preserve relevant email, access, audit and download logs;
- continue a properly scoped investigation;
- provide regular updates and underlying findings;
- take agreed containment and remediation steps; and
- consult the Buyer before notifications, admissions or material communications, subject to legal obligations.

No automatic numeric claim, price deduction, notification obligation or confirmed harm should be assumed on the present evidence. The SPA should preserve rights if later evidence establishes a breach or liability.

---

### 14. Sandbar renewals

**Facts disclosed:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each, AUD 330,000 in total. The disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.

That conclusion is not established by the documents described.

**Pushback:** Assess the contracts, timing, termination rights, service periods, accruals, commitments and accounting treatment. Do not automatically classify the AUD 330,000 as Debt or deduct it from price, but reserve the appropriate treatment under working capital, leakage, ordinary-course covenants or specific completion mechanics once the facts are known.

---

### 15. Tax and IP remain open

**Seller position:** Tax and IP are settled under the general regime.

**Departure:** Our instructions expressly state that Tax and IP terms remain open.

**Pushback:** Reject the assertion of settlement. Review and negotiate the Tax covenant/deed, tax warranties, IP warranties, caps and periods separately. Do not assume either unlimited liability or that these matters fall under the general AUD 4.8 million/18-month regime.

---

### 16. Title evidence

**Seller position:** The internal share register at DD-012 evidences title to 100% of the shares.

**Departure:** DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

**Pushback:** Require corroborating evidence, including as appropriate:

- current independent corporate searches;
- constitution and complete register/history;
- share certificates and transfer/issue records;
- evidence of legal and beneficial ownership;
- searches and releases concerning security interests;
- confirmation of no options, convertible rights or third-party interests; and
- Seller and Company authority approvals.

Independent diligence does not reduce the title warranties or create a Buyer-knowledge defence.

---

### 17. Office lease and Mossvale

The disclosures say the office lease contains a notification obligation rather than a consent requirement, and that the Mossvale restriction concerns assignment rather than a share sale.

These should be verified against the operative provisions, but the present material does not justify automatically demanding consents or making deductions. If the clauses do not contain change-of-control language, the Seller should comply with any actual notice obligation and confirm that the transaction is not an assignment.

## Recommended negotiating position

### Immediate non-negotiable corrections

1. Restore the general cap to **25% / AUD 6 million**.
2. Restore **AUD 5,000 de minimis / AUD 50,000 tipping basket**.
3. Restore the **24-month** general warranty period.
4. Put title/fundamental claims on a **100% cap, at least six-year period**, outside general thresholds and knowledge limitations.
5. Insert the overriding fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out.
6. Delete whole-data-room/public-record deemed disclosure and constructive Buyer knowledge.
7. Prevent the general limitations regime from applying automatically to every type of claim.

### Completion-critical matters

8. Require effective, unconditional or fully satisfied **Bluefen consent** before Completion.
9. Obtain a current **Riverlark payout**, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases at Completion.
10. Add the **AUD 420,000 bonuses plus all on-costs** to the funds flow or otherwise make them expressly Seller-funded.
11. Verify and cure the **Ironquay** payment and IP-transfer issue, supported by a broader specific indemnity.
12. Refresh the Disclosure Letter and diligence record beyond the 22 September 2026 cut-off.

### Matters requiring further diligence rather than assumed conclusions

13. Preserve evidence and complete the **DD-006 incident** investigation without assuming a breach, notification duty, loss or price adjustment.
14. Assess the **Sandbar renewals** without automatically treating them as Debt.
15. Verify the office lease and Mossvale clauses.
16. Obtain independent title and encumbrance evidence.
17. Continue separate negotiations on **Tax and IP**; neither is settled.

1. an effective written Bluefen consent in an agreed form;
2. evidence that all conditions to that consent have been satisfied or irrevocably waived;
3. confirmation that the consent remains effective at Completion; and
4. no materially adverse amendments, concessions or payments without Buyer approval.

The condition should not be deemed satisfied merely on document delivery. The Buyer should control waiver of this condition and retain termination rights if it is not met by the long-stop date.

---

### 10. Riverlark debt and security

**Facts disclosed:** Approximately AUD 3.2 million remains outstanding; the facility has not been repaid and no final security discharge has been provided.

**Seller position:** Release after Completion.

**Departure:** This conflicts with the debt-free/cash-free acquisition basis and our requirement for direct repayment and effective releases at Completion. “Approximately” is not adequate for funds flow.

**Pushback:** Require:

- a current lender payout letter close to Completion;
- repayment directly from Completion funds, with the amount reducing or coming from Seller proceeds;
- repayment of all principal, accrued interest, break costs and fees;
- effective releases and discharges of all guarantees and security at Completion; and
- appropriate filings and control-document deliveries.

A post-Completion release is not acceptable absent an irrevocable lender undertaking in an approved form and Amelia Frost’s express approval. No such approval presently exists.

### 11. Employee Completion bonuses

**Facts disclosed:** AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses; no treatment of payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs; no amount in the funds flow.

**Seller position:** A Seller matter, not separately itemised.

**Risk:** If the Company pays after Completion, the economic burden may silently pass to the Buyer even though the liability arose from the sale.

**Pushback:** Require the bonuses and all triggered employer on-costs to be:

- specifically itemised in the Completion statement/funds flow; and
- funded by the Seller, deducted from Seller proceeds or reimbursed under a specific indemnity.

Confirm which continued-employment conditions will be satisfied at Completion, the identity and amount for each recipient, payment timing and all payroll tax, superannuation and withholding consequences. Avoid double counting with Debt or working-capital mechanics, but do not allow the item to disappear from the economics.

### 12. Ironquay IP

**Facts disclosed:** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but this is not independent verification; there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment.

**Seller position:** Narrow indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment.

**Departure:** Payment alone may not establish that Paperbark owns or may use all relevant IP. The AUD 180,000 figure is not verified.

**Pushback:**

- Obtain direct/current verification of the amount payable.
- Require payment and delivery of an effective assignment or confirmation of ownership/licence as the contractual cure.
- Broaden the indemnity to cover failure to obtain the SOW3 rights, ownership/use defects, third-party claims, additional fees, enforcement and reasonable remediation losses.
- Preserve the SOW3 cure so that the Seller has an opportunity to procure the intended rights, subject to urgency and Buyer control protections.
- Ensure the indemnity is not inadvertently captured by the general warranty cap, basket or period.

The ultimate IP cap and duration remain open; we should not imply agreement to unlimited liability.

### 13. Export/privacy incident

**Facts disclosed:** A download link was sent to an unintended external email address and may relate to about 1,240 records. Access, exact scope, notification obligations and loss are not established.

The disclosure is appropriately cautious. We should neither accept the Seller’s assertion that the matter is immaterial nor characterise it as a confirmed breach.

**Pushback:** Require the Seller and Company to:

- preserve relevant email, access, audit and download logs;
- continue a properly scoped investigation;
- provide regular updates and underlying findings;
- take agreed containment and remediation steps; and
- consult the Buyer before notifications, admissions or material communications, subject to legal obligations.

No automatic numeric claim, price deduction, notification obligation or confirmed harm should be assumed on the present evidence. The SPA should preserve rights if later evidence establishes a breach or liability.

### 14. Sandbar renewals

**Facts disclosed:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each, AUD 330,000 in total. The disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.

That conclusion is not established by the documents described.

**Pushback:** Assess the contracts, timing, termination rights, service periods, accruals, commitments and accounting treatment. Do not automatically classify the AUD 330,000 as Debt or deduct it from price, but reserve the appropriate treatment under working capital, leakage, ordinary-course covenants or specific completion mechanics once the facts are known.

### 15. Tax and IP remain open

**Seller position:** Tax and IP are settled under the general regime.

**Departure:** Our instructions expressly state that Tax and IP terms remain open.

**Pushback:** Reject the assertion of settlement. Review and negotiate the Tax covenant/deed, tax warranties, IP warranties, caps and periods separately. Do not assume either unlimited liability or that these matters fall under the general AUD 4.8 million/18-month regime.

### 16. Title evidence

**Seller position:** The internal share register at DD-012 evidences title to 100% of the shares.

**Departure:** DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

**Pushback:** Require corroborating evidence, including as appropriate:

- current independent corporate searches;
- constitution and complete register/history;
- share certificates and transfer/issue records;
- evidence of legal and beneficial ownership;
- searches and releases concerning security interests;
- confirmation of no options, convertible rights or third-party interests; and
- Seller and Company authority approvals.

Independent diligence does not reduce the title warranties or create a Buyer-knowledge defence.

### 17. Office lease and Mossvale

The disclosures say the office lease contains a notification obligation rather than a consent requirement, and that the Mossvale restriction concerns assignment rather than a share sale.

These should be verified against the operative provisions, but the present material does not justify automatically demanding consents or making deductions. If the clauses do not contain change-of-control language, the Seller should comply with any actual notice obligation and confirm that the transaction is not an assignment.

## Recommended negotiating position

### Immediate non-negotiable corrections

1. Restore the general cap to **25% / AUD 6 million**.
2. Restore **AUD 5,000 de minimis / AUD 50,000 tipping basket**.
3. Restore the **24-month** general warranty period.
4. Put title/fundamental claims on a **100% cap, at least six-year period**, outside general thresholds and knowledge limitations.
5. Insert the overriding fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out.
6. Delete whole-data-room/public-record deemed disclosure and constructive Buyer knowledge.
7. Prevent the general limitations regime from applying automatically to every type of claim.

### Completion-critical matters

8. Require effective, unconditional or fully satisfied **Bluefen consent** before Completion.
9. Obtain a current **Riverlark payout**, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases at Completion.
10. Add the **AUD 420,000 bonuses plus all on-costs** to the funds flow or otherwise make them expressly Seller-funded.
11. Verify and cure the **Ironquay** payment and IP-transfer issue, supported by a broader specific indemnity.
12. Refresh the Disclosure Letter and diligence record beyond the 22 September 2026 cut-off.

### Matters requiring further diligence rather than assumed conclusions

13. Preserve evidence and complete the **DD-006 incident** investigation without assuming a breach, notification duty, loss or price adjustment.
14. Assess the **Sandbar renewals** without automatically treating them as Debt.
15. Verify the office lease and Mossvale clauses.
16. Obtain independent title and encumbrance evidence.
17. Continue separate negotiations on **Tax and IP**; neither is settled.
